notes: RATE FIELDS IN THE SCENARIO EDITOR COULD NOT BE EDITED RELIABLY. REPORTED: changing the land growth rate from 6 to 8 either produced 800 or did not take, and the up/down arrows did nothing. DIAGNOSED, two separate causes. (1) THE IN-APP NUMPAD APPENDS. It intercepts every input of type=number, sets readOnly so the OS keyboard is suppressed — which also disables the native arrows — and its keys APPEND to whatever the field already holds. That suits a money field starting from zero, but on a field pre-filled with 6.0 tapping 8 yields 6.08 rather than 8. (2) THE DECLARED RANGE WAS NOT ENFORCED. HTML min and max are honoured only for user typing, not for values set programmatically, so once the field contained 800 the read stored assetGrowth = 8, meaning 800% a year, which then redisplayed as 800.0. Reproduced precisely before fixing. FIXED: a data-no-numpad opt-out was added to the numpad's focus handler, and both the growth rate and the loan rate now carry it, so small pre-filled percentages keep the native control and its arrows. Independently, both rates are clamped to their declared range on read, before the percent-to-decimal conversion, so an out-of-range value can never reach saved state regardless of how it got into the field. VERIFIED: typing 8 stores 8%; 800 clamps to 30%; -99 clamps to -20%; 8.5 round-trips and redisplays as 8.5; the arrows step correctly; and a loan rate of 850 clamps to 50% rather than becoming 850% a year. The opt-out is a general escape hatch rather than a one-off, so any future field holding a pre-filled non-monetary number can use it. Clamping is applied at the read boundary rather than in the UI, so it holds for every path that writes these fields. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
